subject: Acme DPA — analytics subprocessor and runtime telemetry carveout (product/security sign-off needed)
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: mark.liu@acme.com, legal@acme.com
Date: 2027-09-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redline + analytics subprocessor request

Ben — thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our next pass on the DPA (Acme_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Two items we need explicit alignment on before legal can finalize: 

1) Analytics subprocessor: we need Redwood to confirm that the analytics vendor listed (LogSprite Analytics) will be added as a subprocessors list entry and that they will be limited to aggregated telemetry only (no inference outputs or prompts). Our legal team requires an explicit attestation and a SOC 2 Type II report.

2) Runtime telemetry carveout: we proposed a carveout that allows short-lived runtime traces (up to 7 days) for debugging production incidents, and separate longer-term aggregated telemetry for model/usage analytics. Please confirm retention windows, access controls, and whether KV cache snapshots or prompt-level metadata are excluded from the aggregated dataset.

Can you route to Product and Security for technical sign-off? We want to close this before EOW so we can start the pilot.

—Sarah
Procurement, Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redline_v3.docx (document), subprocessor_inventory_ACME.csv (csv)

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: mark.liu@acme.com, sarah.jenkins@acme.com
Date: 2027-09-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline + analytics subprocessor request — product/security please advise

Looping you all in — Acme surfaced a few redline asks that need Product and Security sign-off. Key asks summarized below (see attached redline):

- Add LogSprite Analytics as a subprocessor with limited scope (aggregated telemetry only). Acme requests SOC2 attestation and a short attestation letter that they do not receive prompts or outputs.
- Allow runtime traces for incident debugging (suggested 7-day retention) but prevent prompt-level or KV cache snapshot export into analytics.

Olga — do you need additional contract language beyond what Acme proposed?
Karthik — can Product confirm the feasibility of preventing KV cache snapshot inclusion in analytics exports and the feasibility of a 7-day debug-only trace that is automatically purged?
Irene — can Security confirm what proof (SOC2, AICPA report, subproc attestation) we can reasonably provide and whether there are additional controls required (KMS/HSM, restricted roles)?

I propose a short triage call today if helpful.

Thanks — Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_changes_summary.txt

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.jenkins@acme.com
Date: 2027-09-01T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + analytics subprocessor request — contract questions

Thanks Ben. Quick legal notes after an initial pass: 

- We can accept a named subprocessor (LogSprite) but legal wants: (a) a subprocessor addendum that includes scope limitations (aggregated telemetry only, no inference outputs or prompts), (b) evidence of SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, and (c) contractual obligation for Redwood to notify Acme of any changes to the subprocessor list 30 days in advance.
- The language around "runtime traces" is ambiguous in the redline. Legal prefers a definition that differentiates (i) ephemeral debug traces (7 days, access limited to on-call engineers for incident remediation), and (ii) aggregated telemetry (90 days default retention, anonymized). We should avoid wording that permits exporting KV cache snapshots or prompt-level debug dumps.

Ask Product to confirm technical constraints and provide suggested language for the DPA that we can offer Acme (e.g., explicit clause: "KV cache snapshots and prompt-level content shall not be included in aggregated telemetry exports or subprocessor processing").

If Product confirms feasibility, Legal can draft the subprocessor addendum and the defined retention windows.

—Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.jenkins@acme.com
Date: 2027-09-01T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + analytics subprocessor request — technical feasibility

Short answer: everything requested is feasible with caveats and a small platform change for explicit export filters. Details: 

- LogSprite as a subprocessor: fine. We can tag telemetry that is "aggregated-analytics-only" at ingestion. That tag prevents routing prompts/outputs to analytics pipelines. We can provide an attestation to Acme about the routing, but SOC2 of LogSprite is external — Security will need to validate acceptable evidence.

- KV cache snapshots: by default we do not export KV cache state. However, there are internal maintenance flows that can snapshot model state for debugging/repairs. We will need to ensure those flows are gated and never included in analytics exports. I propose adding an explicit boolean flag in the export pipeline: include_kv_snapshots = false by default and blocked for partner exports. Implementing the export-filter flag is a 1-sprint change (2 engineers, 3 weeks) for a hardened guardrail and tests.

- Runtime traces: we can support a 7-day debug trace retention scoped to specific incidents, with strict RBAC and audit logs. Aggregated telemetry (metrics/histograms) for model performance can be retained 90 days and withheld from subprocessor feeds unless anonymized and sampled.

Suggested DPA wording product-side: one sentence that prohibits export of prompt-level content and KV cache snapshots to any external subprocessor, plus an operational appendix describing retention, access controls, and the subprocessor attestation process.

If Legal and Security agree, I can scope the engineering ticket and provide a proposed appendix for the DPA.

—Karthik
Director, Product Engineering

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.jenkins@acme.com, mark.liu@acme.com
Date: 2027-09-02T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + analytics subprocessor request — Security sign-off conditions

Summary from Security: we can provisionally sign off on the proposed carveouts provided the following conditions are met and documented in the DPA/subproc addendum: 

1) Subprocessor evidence: LogSprite must provide SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) and a subproc attestation that they will not process or store prompts or inference outputs. Redwood will maintain proof and provide it to Acme upon request.
2) Export controls: explicit clause that KV cache snapshots and prompt-level content are categorically excluded from analytics exports. Any internal snapshotting flows must be auditable; we will require export_filters include_kv_snapshots=false and an automated test in CI.
3) Short-lived traces: runtime traces for debugging limited to 7 days, access limited to named on-call roles, and every access generates an audit entry reviewed weekly for the pilot period.

If Legal drafts the addendum with these items, Security will review and provide a short control-matrix we can append to the DPA. Product's timeline (3 weeks for export filter) is acceptable; Security requests a mitigations plan for the interim during pilot (e.g., manual gating + privileged review).

I'll coordinate with Ops to collect LogSprite SOC2 evidence and provide the required control artifacts. Olga — once you have a draft addendum, please loop Security for a final pass.

—Irene
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
